## 1. Spectral domination does not lift to entropy-loss domination

Let P_N be a lazy reversible bounded-degree expander Markov kernel on N points, with uniform stationary distribution and spectral gap at least γ>0 independent of N. Laziness makes its spectrum nonnegative. Let Π_N reset every input to the uniform distribution. On real functions,

    I−Π_N ≤ γ⁻¹(I−P_N).

This is exactly the kind of universal quadratic/Dirichlet comparison furnished by the common spectral comparator.

For a point mass δ_x, however,

    D(δ_x||u)−D(Π_Nδ_x||u)=lnN.

The support of P_Nδ_x has at most d+1 points if the underlying graph degree is d, so

    D(δ_x||u)−D(P_Nδ_x||u)=H(P_Nδ_x)≤ln(d+1).

Thus no universal constant can pass this quadratic comparison through relative entropy for the SAME comparator Π_N. The ratio grows at least lnN/ln(d+1).

This is not a counterexample to existence of another EB comparator: the identity channel on a classical algebra is already EB and has zero entropy loss. It proves that the checked C4 inequality alone cannot establish the proposed entropy theorem by applying a scalar/operator functional calculus to its quadratic forms.

## 2. The precise tree obstruction

The existing proof constructs unbiased leaf estimators z and controls their covariance through an exact sibling second-moment recursion. Its regression step is quadratic. A relative-entropy variational argument instead requires control of exponential moments of those estimators.

Even for commuting random variables with identical marginals, arbitrary sibling dependence gives only the Hölder bound

    E exp[(z_1+...+z_r)/r] ≤ E exp(z_1).

There is no independent-product factorization and no automatic 1/r improvement in the logarithmic moment-generating function. Covariance bounds do not repair this: rare perfectly correlated large outcomes can have bounded covariance while making exponential moments arbitrarily large.

The spectral threshold also hides a concrete information issue. A bounded-degree expander can have every nonconstant eigenvalue below the C4 supercritical threshold, so the spectral construction is allowed to return Π_N, while one channel use still retains lnN−O(1) bits about a uniform point input. ## Exact local necessary condition

For ρ_t=σ+tA, TrA=0 and A Hermitian, the relative entropy Hessian is

    D(ρ_t||σ)=(t²/2) Tr[A Ωσ⁻¹(A)]+O(t³),
    Ωσ⁻¹(A)=∫₀∞ (σ+sI)⁻¹ A (σ+sI)⁻¹ ds.

Thus the proposed comparator necessarily obeys, as quadratic forms on traceless Hermitian perturbations,

    Ωσ⁻¹−Ψ*Ωσ⁻¹Ψ ≤ K(Ωσ⁻¹−Φ*Ωσ⁻¹Φ).

This is the Bogoliubov–Kubo–Mori metric. It is not the sandwiched Rényi-2 metric used by the checked C4 proof. In an eigenbasis of σ, the coefficient on A_ij is

    c(σ_i,σ_j)=(lnσ_i−lnσ_j)/(σ_i−σ_j),

with c(a,a)=1/a.

## Thermal-qubit test: no counterexample, exact local constant 2

Let σ=diag(1−s,s), 0<s<1, and Φ be generalized amplitude damping with relaxation γ=1/2 and stationary excitation s. It is a convex mixture of zero-temperature downward and upward amplitude damping channels at damping 1/2, each of which has a symmetric two-output extension. Hence Φ is self-compatible. It fixes σ, is positive and selfadjoint in the relevant diagonal KMS coordinates, acts on population perturbations by 1/2, and on both real and imaginary coherences by 1/√2.

Let Ψ dephase in the σ eigenbasis. Its entropy-loss Hessian vanishes on population perturbations and equals the full BKM form on coherences. For Φ, the corresponding loss fractions are 3/4 on populations and 1/2 on coherences. Consequently the local necessary condition holds with K=2, uniformly as s→0. Extremely small eigenvalues alone do not break the local conjecture.

## Why fixed σ-eigenbasis pinching is not a general answer

A σ-preserving EB Petz measurement channel can retain almost all of a noncommuting X direction when σ is close to maximally mixed, while pinching in a fixed nondegenerate σ eigenbasis destroys that direction. The comparator must be allowed to choose a POVM adapted to Φ; σ-basis dephasing is not universally sufficient.

## A tempting modular gain that self-compatibility blocks in the two-level model

A generic coherence map that sends a pair of reference weights (a,b) to (ta,b) and attenuates the coherence by √t has BKM retention ratio

    t c(ta,b)/c(a,b) → 1 + ln(t)/ln(a/b)

when a/b→∞. Hence a single channel can appear to retain nearly all BKM information while attenuating an amplitude by a constant.

## Exact example

For 0<r≤1 take the uniform six-state qubit ensemble

    E_r={ρ_(j,s)=(I+s r σ_j)/2 : j∈{x,y,z}, s∈{−1,+1}}.

Its optimal prior-average reconstruction error over a single entanglement-breaking channel is exactly

    e_p(E_r)=r/3.

Proof: twirl any EB channel by the octahedral rotation group, simultaneously acting on input and output. Convexity of trace distance and invariance of the ensemble show that average error does not increase. The twirled channel has zero translation and scalar Bloch matrix tI. For a depolarizing qubit channel, EB implies t≤1/3: its normalized Choi state is t|Φ><Φ|+(1−t)I/4, and partial transpose has eigenvalue (1−3t)/4. Conversely t=1/3 is EB, explicitly choose one Pauli basis uniformly, measure in that basis, and reprepare the measured eigenstate. The error is r|1−t|/2, minimized at t=1/3.

The channel

    T(ρ)=(2/3)ρ+(1/3)I/2

is self-compatible. A full-domain symmetric extension is

    B(ρ)=(2/3)P_sym(ρ⊗I)P_sym,
    P_sym=(I+SWAP)/2.

Indeed it is CP; Tr[P_sym(ρ⊗I)]=3/2; and each partial trace is (2/3)ρ+(1/6)I. Thus both marginals equal T.

Let h(q)=−q ln q−(1−q)ln(1−q). The ensemble averages before and after T are I/2, hence

    δ_r=χ(E_r)−χ(T(E_r))
       =h((1+2r/3)/2)−h((1+r)/2)
       =(5/18)r²+O(r⁴).

Consequently, any universal bound

    e_p(E)≤K[χ(E)−χ(T(E))]^α

for all self-compatible T and finite ensembles must satisfy α≤1/2. If α=1/2, then K≥sqrt(2/5). This does NOT disprove any exponent 0<α≤1/2, nor the existence of a dimension-free modulus.

## A genuine literature implication, and the missing implication

Seshadreesan and Wilde, Physical Review A 92, 042321, Proposition 32 (approximate faithfulness), establish small quantum discord implies approximate invariance under one EB channel. Their explicit natural-log-compatible estimate is halftrace error at most sqrt(discord), up to log-base conventions. Piani, PRL 117, 080401, gives a hierarchy of symmetric-broadcast recoverability quantities below the EB recoverability quantity and quantum discord.

Primary sources:
- https://link.aps.org/accepted/10.1103/PhysRevA.92.042321
- https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.06855
- https://pure.strath.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/53822980/Piani_PRL2016_Hierarchy_of_efficiently_computable_and_faithful_lower_bounds_to_quantum_discord.pdf
